newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh business world approves of India's Gujral.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh business world approves of India's Gujral.

text.p: Bangladesh on Sunday declined official comment on the likelihood of Inder Kumar Gujral becoming new Prime Minister of India, but the business community called it a "positive development."
Officials said they would wait until Gujral, whom they privately described as a man of vision and friend of Bangladesh, actually takes over from outgoing Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Some said initial reactions could be available after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina returned home on Monday after the Haj pilgrimage to Mecca.
But Yusuf Abdullah Harun, president of the Federation of Bangladesh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said "Mr Gujral's choice is a good news for us and possibly for all of India's neighbours."
"He knows the region very closely and has had promoted friendly ties with (neighbours)," Harun told Reuters.
"I believe the relationship between our two countries will be stronger, especially in the field of economic cooperation.
"Gujral has been long associated with developments in Bangladesh. He is a very reasonable and balanced man."
Dr. Q. K. Ahmed, chairman of Bangladesh Unnayon Parishad (development council), expressed his "full satisfaction" over Gijral's nomination to succeed Deve Gowda.

He recalled Gujral's contributions to a 30-year treaty India and Bangladesh had signed in December for sharing water from the Ganges river, that ended a decades-old dispute between the two unequal neighbours.

During Deve Gowda's 10-month rule, the two countries also reached agreements to repatriate up to 50,000 Bangladeshi tribal refugees from the northeast Indian state of Tripura and to help each other to fight insurgents.
Bangladesh and India are also partners in a four-nation sub-regional economic cooperation bloc and the South Asia Development Triangle, proposed by the World Bank.
"Bangladesh was really worried over the fall of Deve Gowda's government and uncertainties over his successor," said independent analyst Matiur Rahman Chowdhury.
"Although the dust over India's political future has yet to settle, we were relieved that Deve Gowda's close confidant is the most likely successor," he said.
